properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-17, from Space Force capability development: designing against an adversary's deny/degrade/disrupt/destroy, with new intelligence arriving constantly — "we would start designing something and then we would find that the adversary was doing something else and we would have to adjust the design." His own framing of the general case: "the design was always evolving based on some new factor that hadn't been there when we first designed it."

⭐ THE ASYMMETRY THAT NAMES THE GAP. reflow2's `propagate_change` answers *what does this DESIGN change touch?* His domain needs *what does this WORLD change touch?* — and those are different questions, because the design graph is CLOSED UNDER ITSELF. Every node reflow2 can reason about is part of the design. External reality enters only as observations ABOUT the design — drift, verification, reconciliation — never as PREMISES the design rests on. So an assumption about an adversary, a competitor, a regulator or a supplier is invisible: it shaped the design and is not in it.

⇒ THE QUESTION IN ONE LINE: **when the intel is revised, can you find everything you built on it?** Today, no. There is nothing to propagate from.

⭐⭐ AND THE MECHANISM IS ONE STEP AWAY, WHICH IS THE INTERESTING PART. `set_requirement_lineage` already declares `derived` — "technical necessity nobody asked for, created by a design decision — pair it with governed_by to that Decision" — and its own description states the consequence that matters here: **"a derived requirement may lose its reason to exist if the decision behind it is re-opened."** That is EXACTLY the semantics he needs, already built, and pointed at an INTERNAL cause. The gap is that reflow2 models "derived from a decision we made" and has no notion of "derived from a fact about the world."

MEASURED ON REFLOW2'S OWN GRAPH, 2026-08-17, and the numbers argue against reaching for new vocabulary first:
    EVOLVES_INTO edges in use     0
    SUPERSEDES                    0
    SUPPLEMENTS                   0
    MITIGATES                     0
    TRIGGERS                      0
    MASKS                         0
    RISKS                         1
    EnvironmentRule nodes         0
    Requirement `lineage`         176 of 176 `original` — `derived` and `decomposed` NEVER USED
So the evolution vocabulary AND the threat vocabulary already exist and are almost entirely unexercised. Declared and never written to is the trap `req:a-finding-has-somewhere-to-put-its-evidence` names explicitly, and adding a node type here without understanding why the existing ones went unused would repeat it at a larger scale. ⇒ See `dec:idea-is-the-evolution-vocabulary-unused-because-nothing-asks-for-it`.

THE SHAPES, none chosen:
(A) A TemporalFact IS ALREADY THIS, USED DIFFERENTLY. It is a time-bounded assertion with `subject_id`, `valid_from`/`valid_to`, and `basis: measured | forecast`. An intel assessment is a forecast about a subject with a validity window; when it expires or is superseded, everything pointing at it is the blast radius. COST: `subject_id` points INTO the design, so a fact about an adversary has no subject to name — the shape fits and the anchor does not.
(B) THE PREMISE IS AN ASSUMPTION NODE, and design elements DEPEND_ON it. Cleanest propagation story: revising the assumption walks the existing machinery. COST: new node type, and reflow2 has been careful about that.
(C) THE ADVERSARY IS AN ACTOR. An Actor is "who the designed system serves" — an adversary is the anti-Actor, and their capabilities could hang off them. COST: inverts the type's meaning; and reflow2 holds only 3 Actors, so the type is barely exercised either.
(D) DON'T MODEL THE WORLD — model the DEPENDENCE. Do not try to hold what the adversary can do; hold only "requirement D exists BECAUSE of external premise P", where P is a named, dated, citable claim and nothing more. Cheapest, and it is the half that makes the blast radius computable. The design never pretends to model the threat.
(E) NOT REFLOW2'S JOB. Intel and market analysis live in their own systems; reflow2 records the design. COST: then the "why did we build this?" answer permanently leaves the graph, which is the thing he says was hardest.

⚠️ THE HONEST BOUND WHICHEVER WAY THIS GOES: reflow2 cannot tell you the adversary changed. It can only tell you what you built on the belief that they had not — which is the same class of limit as `dec:non-goal-reflow2-does-not-know-what-is-deprecated`, and worth stating in the same breath as the capability.

📌 WHY THIS IS NOT NICHE. Every long-lived design has premises that move: a regulation, a supplier, a platform version, a competitor, a funding line, a user population. Space Force is the sharpest instance because the premise is adversarial and therefore moves ON PURPOSE. NSLS-II has the same shape with a decade-old stack underneath it.
properties.name: OPEN — reflow2 computes the blast radius of a DESIGN change; can it compute the blast radius of a WORLD change, when the premise a design rested on turns out to have moved?
properties.rationale: Recorded as brainstorming. reflow2's graph is closed under itself: external reality enters only as observations about the design, never as premises the design rests on — so when an assumption is revised there is nothing to propagate from. The mechanism is one step away rather than absent: `lineage: derived` already means "may lose its reason to exist if the decision behind it is re-opened", pointed at an internal cause. But the evolution and threat vocabulary already present is measured at 0/0/0/0/0/1 uses, so understanding why it went unused should precede adding more.
